skill.name: golang-benchmark
skill.description: Guides Go benchmark design, statistical comparison, CPU and memory profiling, trace analysis, compiler diagnostics, and CI performance regression detection.
skill.summary: Measure Go performance with reproducible benchmarks, profiles, traces, and statistical comparisons.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are lexical false positives caused by Markdown, localhost examples, and profiling terminology. Confirmed risks include privileged CPU controls, token delegation, and an unauthenticated all-interface trace viewer. Semantic review also found insecure TLS guidance and an unpinned tool installation.

remediation.issue: Benchmark setup commands modify host-wide CPU controls with sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, use dedicated ephemeral runners, record previous values, and provide restoration commands.

remediation.issue: A third-party GitHub Action receives GITHUB_TOKEN.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the action to a commit SHA and declare only the minimum required repository permissions.

remediation.issue: The trace viewer example binds to every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Bind to loopback by default and require authenticated tunneling for remote access.

remediation.issue: A pprof example disables TLS certificate verification.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the insecure example or require verified certificates and an explicit warning for exceptional use.

remediation.issue: The benchstat installation uses a mutable latest version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed benchstat version in metadata and installation instructions.

content.value_statement: Go performance work often fails because benchmarks are noisy or profiles are misread. This skill provides a rigorous workflow for measurement, comparison, and diagnosis.
actual_capabilities: Designs Go benchmarks with correct setup, timing, allocation tracking, and sub-benchmark structure.
Runs repeated benchmarks and interprets benchstat confidence intervals, p-values, and normalized metrics.
Guides CPU, heap, goroutine, mutex, and block profile collection with pprof.
Explains Go execution traces for scheduling, blocking, garbage collection, and latency analysis.
Uses compiler diagnostics for escape analysis, inlining, SSA, and assembly inspection.
Outlines CI regression checks and reproducible benchmark conditions.
limitations: It cannot eliminate hardware, thermal, virtualization, or background workload noise.
It does not replace production load testing or application-specific performance requirements.
Profile interpretation still requires representative workloads and symbols from the measured build.
Some runner tuning examples require Linux, dedicated hardware, and elevated privileges.

use_cases.title: Validate an Optimization
use_cases.description: Create repeatable before-and-after benchmarks and decide whether measured changes are statistically significant.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Production Latency
use_cases.description: Correlate runtime metrics with CPU, memory, goroutine, and trace evidence to identify expensive paths.

use_cases.title: Prevent CI Regressions
use_cases.description: Establish benchmark baselines, practical thresholds, and controlled runner settings for pull request checks.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Go benchmark for [function]. Exclude setup time, report allocations, and use representative inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these baseline and candidate benchmark results. Explain significance, noise, allocation changes, and whether the optimization is supported.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this [CPU or memory] profile summary. Identify likely application callers and recommend focused pprof commands for confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Regression Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI benchmark gate for [repository]. Include baseline handling, sample counts, thresholds, runner controls, permissions, and failure investigation.

output_examples.input: A candidate benchmark is three percent faster, but benchstat reports no significant difference.
output_examples.output: Do not claim an improvement. Increase sample quality, control environmental noise, and compare both versions under identical conditions.

output_examples.input: A CPU profile is dominated by runtime allocation functions.
output: Rank cumulative callers to find application entry points.
Inspect hot source lines and collect an allocation profile.
Confirm escape behavior before changing allocation strategy.

output_examples.input: CI benchmarks vary by ten percent between runs.
output_examples.output: Use a dedicated runner, run benchmarks serially, increase repetitions, and set thresholds above measured environmental variance.

best_practices: Compare versions on the same toolchain, hardware, workload, and runner configuration.
Collect multiple samples and use statistical results before making performance claims.
Preserve benchmark context, profile type, build identity, and hardware details with every result.
anti_patterns: Do not approve an optimization from one benchmark run or a nonsignificant result.
Do not run competing benchmarks concurrently on shared processors.
Do not expose profiling or trace endpoints without authentication and network restrictions.

faq.question: Does this skill write Go benchmarks?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides benchmark structure, timing boundaries, allocation reporting, sub-benchmarks, and representative inputs.

faq.question: Can it interpret benchstat output?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains medians, confidence intervals, p-values, sample counts, and nonsignificant comparisons.

faq.question: Which profiles does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CPU, heap, allocation, goroutine, mutex, block, and trace-derived profiles.

faq.question: Can it diagnose production issues?
faq.answer: It can guide evidence collection and interpretation, but results depend on representative traffic and secure profiling access.

faq.question: Does it support CI regression detection?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents benchmark gates, trend storage, thresholds, and runner controls for stable comparisons.

faq.question: Does system tuning require administrator access?
faq.answer: Some Linux CPU controls require elevated privileges and should run only on dedicated, recoverable benchmark hosts.
